title: Constant-Stepsize Stochastic Approximation: Finite-Time Convergence, Gaussian Approximation, and Tail Bounds
abstract: arXiv:2602.13960v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Constant-stepsize stochastic approximation (SA) is widely used in learning for computational efficiency, yet the distribution of the iterates is typically intractable. Classical asymptotics results give $X_k^{(\alpha)} \approx X^{(\alpha)} \approx x^\star+\sqrt{\alpha}Y$, where $X^{(\alpha)}$ is the steady state and $Y$ is an appropriate Gaussian limit, by progressively taking the time $k\uparrow\infty$ and stepsize $\alpha\downarrow0$. Such limit results, however, do not quantify finite-time, finite-stepsize errors.   We develop an explicit pre-limit characterization for SA with i.i.d.\ and Markovian noise. We establish existence and uniqueness of the stationary law, a geometric Wasserstein convergence to stationarity, and almost-sure and $L^3$ convergence of the steady state to the root $x^\star$, identifying the scale $\sqrt{\alpha}$ as first-order fluctuation. translated_title: 恒定步长随机逼近：有限时间收敛、高斯近似与尾界
translated_abstract: 恒定步长随机逼近（SA）因其在计算效率方面的优势而在学习领域被广泛使用，然而其迭代点的分布通常难以解析处理。经典的渐近结果给出了 $X_k^{(\alpha)} \approx X^{(\alpha)} \approx x^\star+\sqrt{\alpha}Y$，其中 $X^{(\alpha)}$ 为稳态，$Y$ 为相应的高斯极限，这是通过令时间 $k\uparrow\infty$ 和步长 $\alpha\downarrow0$ 逐步逼近得到的。然而，这类极限结果并未量化有限时间、有限步长下的误差。我们针对具有独立同分布噪声和马尔可夫噪声的SA发展了一种显式的极限前刻画。我们建立了平稳分布的存在性与唯一性、以几何速率收敛到平稳态的Wasserstein收敛性，以及稳态到根 $x^\star$ 的几乎必然收敛和 $L^3$ 收敛，并确定了 $\sqrt{\alpha}$ 作为一阶波动的尺度。在该尺度上，我们推导了高阶定量高斯近似……
tldr: 该论文为独立同分布和马尔可夫噪声下的恒定步长随机逼近建立了显式的极限前理论刻画，证明了平稳分布的存在唯一性及几何Wasserstein收敛速率，并在 $\sqrt{\alpha}$ 波动尺度上推导出高阶定量高斯近似与尾界，从而量化了经典渐近结果无法捕捉的有限时间、有限步长误差。
en_tdlr: This paper develops an explicit pre-limit characterization of constant-stepsize stochastic approximation with i.i.d. and Markovian noise, establishing existence and uniqueness of the stationary law with geometric Wasserstein convergence, and deriving higher-order quantitative Gaussian approximation and tail bounds at the √α fluctuation scale to quantify finite-time, finite-stepsize errors beyond classical asymptotics.
